key_facts: UK teledermatology is mostly **store-and-forward**: advice and guidance, or images on all **suspected-cancer skin referrals**.
Image standard: **three views**: regional (where), close-up with ruler, and **dermoscopic**.
Good images let specialists triage, reassure or fast-track and avoid wasted appointments.
Pitfalls: poor focus, glare, no scale, wrong lesion, missing history; images can't be palpated.
Consent, secure systems and record-keeping are required.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.h: Image standards (BAD/PCDS/Primary Care Dermatology quality standards)

ul: **Three views:** a regional/whole-site image (anatomical location), a close-up with a **ruler/scale**, and a **dermoscopic image** (polarised, in focus, the whole lesion in view).

Good lighting, no flash glare, a plain background, a labelled patient ID, consent, and secure NHS-approved systems (**no personal phones/WhatsApp** without an approved app and policy). Include history (duration, change, symptoms, 7-point score, risk factors, Fitzpatrick type).

blocks: For lesion triage, accuracy is comparable to face-to-face assessment for many lesions when dermoscopic images are of good quality. It reduces unnecessary face-to-face appointments and speeds up the management of cancers. Image quality is the main failure mode. Darker skin types are under-represented in training.
Nodular/amelanotic melanoma can be under-called on. Teledermatology must not delay a 2WW-meeting referral; where a pathway uses, they **accompany** the urgent referral rather than replace it.
